title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From UCLA Health (2026)
summary: Every UCLA Health form, phone number, fax, and address you need to request medical records in 2026, plus the department routing and fee rules that keep requests from bouncing back.
body_markdown:
UCLA Health runs one of the largest academic medical systems in Southern California, including Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center, UCLA Medical Center Santa Monica, Jules Stein Eye Institute, and Resnick Neuropsychiatric Hospital. For personal injury attorneys, getting records means knowing which department to contact and which form to submit. UCLA[routes certain records](https://www.uclahealth.org/patient-resources/medical-records) to separate departments, so it's easy to send a request to the wrong place and wait weeks for nothing.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) manages the whole retrieval process, from authorization validation to persistent follow-up across UCLA's departments.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


UCLA Health processes record requests within[15 business days](https://www.uclahealth.org/patient-resources/support-information/medical-records/frequently-asked-questions) of receipt


-


Three request pathways: myUCLAhealth, a secure online authorization, or the downloadable form by email, fax, or mail


-


[UCLA Form #30910](https://www.uclahealth.org/sites/default/files/documents/Authorization-for-release-of-health-Info-English_1.pdf) defaults to expiring 12 months after signing when the expiration field is blank, and UCLA does not accept electronic signatures on it


-


Resnick accepts authorizations by email, but neuropsychiatric records are not delivered by email


-


Arthur Ashe Student Health holds Ashe Center records for appointments before July 8, 2025


-


Fees depend on the legal basis; patients requesting their own records are told there is no fee


-


Codes Health validates authorizations before submission, follows up across channels, and verifies completeness before delivery


## **Understanding the UCLA Health Medical Records Request Process**


### **Why You Might Need Your UCLA Health Records**


PI cases need documentation to establish damages, prove causation, and support demand calculations: emergency department visits, specialist consultations and imaging, surgical and hospitalization records, billing statements, and mental health treatment documentation.


The complication is that UCLA keeps separate departments for different record types. A general request to Health Information Management Services (HIMS) won't pull mental health, dental, or radiology images without additional contacts.


### **Overview of the Request Journey**


UCLA describes[three request options](https://www.uclahealth.org/patient-resources/medical-records) : request through myUCLAhealth or MyStudentChart, complete a secure online authorization, or download the paper form and submit it by email, fax, or mail. UCLA says requests are processed within 15 business days of receipt, and that unsigned or incomplete requests will not be processed and will be returned.


That return-and-resubmit cycle is where firms lose time, and incomplete or defective authorizations are a leading preventable cause of rejected requests.


Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that otherwise cause rejections. It's built for the authorization requirements health systems like UCLA enforce.


## **Navigating UCLA Health's Official Medical Records Request Form**


### **Key Sections of the Request Form**


[UCLA Form #30910](https://www.uclahealth.org/sites/default/files/documents/Authorization-for-release-of-health-Info-English_1.pdf) is a two-page fillable PDF with multiple sections to complete. Always download the current version from UCLA's medical records page, since the live PDF has carried inconsistent revision markings across its two pages.


-


**Patient Information:** full legal name, Medical Record Number (MRN), date of birth, and current address, phone, and email


-


**Healthcare Facility:** UCLA Health Hospitals/Clinics (specify doctor or clinic), Jules Stein Eye Institute, Resnick Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Arthur Ashe Student Wellness Center, or Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS)


-


**Records Release Destination:** recipient name (hospital, clinic, person, or law firm), mailing address, phone and fax, and an email address for request-status updates


-


**Delivery Format Selection:** CD (the form's default when the field is blank), email (not used for neuropsychiatric and behavioral health records), or paper copy


**Record Types Requested:**


-


Clinic visits (office notes and consultations)


-


Emergency reports and discharge summaries


-


Laboratory, pathology, and operative reports


-


Radiology reports and images


-


History and physical exams, and billing statements


-


Mental health records (requires explicit authorization)


### **Avoiding Common Form-Related Delays**


The errors that most often send a request back:


-


**Missing signatures:** Signature and date are both required, and UCLA does not accept electronic signatures on the downloadable form


-


**Incomplete date ranges:** Specify exact FROM and TO dates in MM/DD/YYYY format


-


**Unchecked sensitive information boxes:** Drug and alcohol abuse results, HIV/AIDS results, genetic testing, and psychological test results need explicit checkbox authorization when requested


-


**Wrong facility specification:** A general request won't retrieve specialty records


One point worth knowing: if the expiration field is blank, UCLA's current form defaults to 12 months after the signature date, so a blank expiration doesn't by itself make the authorization incomplete. Using UCLA's current form reduces the risk of omitting UCLA-specific information.


Codes Health validates every authorization before submission, checking date ranges, facility information, and provider-specific requirements.


## **HIPAA Authorization: Essential for UCLA Health Record Releases**


### **Understanding HIPAA Regulations at UCLA Health**


For a typical patient-authorized release to a law firm or other third party, the authorization has to satisfy HIPAA requirements under 45 CFR § 164.508:


-


Clear identification of the information to be disclosed


-


Identification of the person or entity authorized to receive it


-


Description of the purpose of the disclosure


-


An expiration date or event


-


Patient signature and date


HIPAA also permits certain disclosures without a patient authorization in circumstances the Privacy Rule defines, so not every release runs through § 164.508. Patients may revoke an authorization in writing through UCLA Health HIMS.


### **Who Can Authorize a Release?**


A valid authorization can come from:


-


The patient directly


-


A personal representative whose currently effective legal authority covers the relevant healthcare decisions or record access


-


A parent or guardian who is the minor's legally recognized[personal representative](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/personal-representatives-and-minors/index.html) , subject to exceptions


A generic financial power of attorney does not automatically confer[HIPAA access rights](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/does-having-health-care-power-attorney-allow-access-patients-medical-mental-health-records-under-hipaa/index.html) ; the document has to grant healthcare authority and be effective under applicable law.


Records may also be obtainable through judicial process, such as a court order or qualifying subpoena, subject to HIPAA's[judicial proceedings provisions](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/judicial-and-administrative-proceedings/index.html) and state law. That route is separate from a patient-signed authorization and doesn't make the attorney a personal representative.


When someone other than the patient signs, UCLA requires documentation of that person's legal authority, such as an Advance Directive or Power of Attorney. A law firm named as recipient does not become the personal representative merely by receiving records. Codes Health manages authorization workflows end to end while respecting each system's signature rules, including UCLA's position on electronic signatures.

### **When to Call vs. When to Mail**

Provide an email address where the form asks for one, since that's where UCLA sends request-status communications. UCLA also says it will not fax copies of records to a home or business fax, so don't plan on a return fax for delivery.

## **Accessing Your UCLA Health Medical Records Online (MyChart and Portals)**


### **Setting Up Your UCLA Health MyChart Account**


The[myUCLAhealth patient portal](https://www.uclahealth.org/patient-resources/myuclahealth) is the quickest route for patients requesting their own records. Sign-up uses identity verification, and two-step verification is supported. UCLA publishes no separate, faster processing guarantee for portal requests; its figure is 15 business days of receipt.


**Self-Service Record Access (No Authorization Needed):** visit history and appointment summaries, laboratory results and radiology reports, medications, immunizations, allergies, discharge summaries, progress notes, and billing statements.


**Technical Support:** (855) 364-7052 (24/7)


### **What Records are Available Through Online Portals?**


myUCLAhealth provides access to portions of a patient's health information, including many test results and clinical records. Mental health records, certain sensitive information, and records requiring certification may not be available for download. UCLA also states that the record request function can only be accessed by PC, with mobile devices not currently supported.


For matters requiring a complete record set, firms shouldn't assume the documents visible in the portal represent every responsive record. Codes Health works through provider portals, including UCLA's, alongside traditional channels.


## **Requesting Older or Archival Medical Records from UCLA Health**


### **Special Considerations for Older Records**


PI cases often need records spanning years, and older records may sit in different systems or with different custodians, so confirm the right department before submitting. As of[July 8, 2025](https://www.studenthealth.ucla.edu/medrecords) , Ashe Center records moved onto UCLA Health's system, which changes where a request goes depending on when treatment occurred.


### **UCLA Health's Record Retention Guidelines**


**Ashe Center Records Transition:**


-


Appointments on or after July 8, 2025: UCLA Health HIMS


-


Appointments before July 8, 2025: Arthur Ashe Student Health


-

**Arthur Ashe Student Health (Pre-July 8, 2025 Records):**

**Fee:** None for current and past students; $15 for third-party requests

## **Medical Records Release Form Template for UCLA Health Requests**


### **Customizing a Template for Specific Needs**


Form #30910 is the authorization for downloadable paper requests, and firms can build workflow templates around it: pre-fill firm name, address, phone, and fax in the recipient section, include the record types PI cases usually need, and keep separate templates by case type with client instructions for the patient sections.


### **Where to Find Reliable Templates**


Use the current form linked on the[UCLA Health medical](https://www.uclahealth.org/patient-resources/medical-records) records page. UCLA also offers a secure online authorization and the myUCLAhealth route, so the paper form isn't the only mechanism available.


## **Ensuring Completeness: What to Do After Receiving Records from UCLA Health**


### **Checking for Missing Dates or Visits**


Receiving records is the first step, not the last. Common gaps:


-


Date ranges missing from within the requested period


-


Absent billing records when medical records are present


-


Missing radiology images when reports reference imaging


-


Incomplete specialist consultation notes


-


Missing emergency department records from initial treatment


### **How to Address Incomplete Records from UCLA Health**


If records look incomplete, contact[UCLA Health HIMS](https://www.uclahealth.org/patient-resources/medical-records) at (310) 825-6021, ready to name which dates, facilities, or record types are missing.


Codes Health checks delivered records against the original request and available patient history, resolving gaps with UCLA before returning the set. That verified completeness step helps firms judge whether a record set is genuinely complete.


## **UCLA Health Record Fees and No-Cost Exceptions**


Fees depend on the legal basis and who is asking, so the two regimes shouldn't be blended.


Patients requesting their own UCLA records are told there is[no fee](https://www.uclahealth.org/patient-resources/support-information/medical-records/frequently-asked-questions) . For patient access generally, California Health & Safety Code § 123110 permits a reasonable, cost-based fee with paper copies capped at $0.25 per page and microfilm at $0.50.


For attorney pre-litigation requests, California[Evidence Code § 1158](https://law.justia.com/codes/california/code-evid/division-9/chapter-3/section-1158/) sets its own cost provisions: $0.10 per standard page, $0.20 per microfilm page, clerical costs capped at $16 per hour in the circumstances it covers, postage, and certain third-party retrieval costs.


UCLA may invoice third-party requestors, but its FAQ directs them to its invoice payment system without publishing a fee schedule, so confirm charges with HIMS rather than assuming a rate. Payment goes to "UC REGENTS" through the[online payment portal](https://commerce.cashnet.com/42859PAY) or by mail.


California also provides a limited no-charge right to relevant records for specified public-benefit claims or appeals, covering programs such as Medi-Cal, IHSS, CalWORKs, SSDI, SSI/SSP, CalFresh, and qualifying veterans benefits, subject to statutory conditions. One limitation matters here: the[Medical Board of California](https://www.mbc.ca.gov/Resources/Medical-Resources/Access-Records.aspx) states the provision doesn't apply where a private attorney is paying the costs of the claim or appeal pending its outcome, so it isn't automatic for law firm requests.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How long does it take to get medical records from UCLA Health?**


UCLA Health states that requests are processed within[15 business days](https://www.uclahealth.org/patient-resources/support-information/medical-records/frequently-asked-questions) of receipt, and publishes no faster window for myUCLAhealth requests. STAT requests, available to physicians and hospitals only, get priority handling. Unsigned or incomplete requests are returned unprocessed, which is why validating forms first matters.


### **Can I request medical records for a family member from UCLA Health?**


Yes, with documentation of your legal authority. When someone other than the patient signs, UCLA requires proof such as a Power of Attorney, court-appointed guardianship, or Advance Directive designation. Parents or legal guardians can generally request a minor child's records when they are the legally recognized personal representative, subject to exceptions. A power of attorney has to cover healthcare decisions or record access.


### **Is there a fee to obtain medical records from UCLA Health?**


Patients requesting their own records are told there is[no fee](https://www.uclahealth.org/patient-resources/support-information/medical-records/frequently-asked-questions) . Other charges depend on the legal basis: attorney pre-litigation requests fall under California Evidence Code § 1158, while patient access is governed by Health & Safety Code § 123110. UCLA directs third-party requestors to its invoice payment system without publishing a universal fee schedule, so confirm charges before submitting.


### **What if I need my UCLA Health records urgently?**


STAT requests are available only to physicians and hospitals with urgent medical needs, by fax to (310) 206-4831. For legal matters with approaching deadlines, call HIMS directly. If authorization delays persist, judicial process may be an alternative route, subject to HIPAA and state law.


### **How do I correct an error in my UCLA Health medical record?**


Submit a written amendment request to UCLA Health HIMS naming the information you believe is incorrect and the correction you want. HIPAA generally requires action within 60 days, with one possible extension of up to 30 additional days when the rule's requirements are met. UCLA advises that amendment requests may take roughly 60 to 90 days.


### **Does UCLA Health offer different contact information for radiology images versus written reports?**


Yes. Written radiology reports come through main HIMS, but the actual images (X-rays, MRIs, CTs) require contacting the Radiology Film Library directly: Westwood at (310) 825-6425, Santa Monica at (424) 259-8111. Ophthalmology images from Jules Stein Eye Institute require the Ophthalmology Call Center at (310) 825-5000.
